key_insight: SAG-Mem preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks to support long-term conversational memory. It targets questions whose answers require combining facts across sessions, including evidence that does not closely resemble the question.
problem_solved: Relevant facts can be scattered across conversations, and similarity-based retrieval may miss intermediate evidence. Derived memory representations and persistent relational structures can also add construction costs and lose source details.
method: Preserve complete dialogue messages rather than relying solely on derived memory representations.
Organize messages into non-overlapping chunks for retrieval.
Target complementary evidence across dialogue sessions; the provided abstract is truncated before explaining the discovery mechanism.
impact: For practitioners building conversational assistants, SAG-Mem offers a source-preserving approach to long-term memory. The supplied excerpt does not include evaluation results, so performance and efficiency gains cannot be assessed.
